provenance: Computed by the LunarWindow pipeline from NASA LOLA terrain and NASA SPICE (DE421) ephemerides. Code written with AI assistance (Claude Code) and verified by the team with automated tests and a comparison against NASA PGDA illumination maps.
verdict: Touchdown 2028-09-01T09 UTC: the Sun's centre is 0.58 deg above the skyline and the top of Earth's disc 1.15 deg above the skyline (power and a link at landing).
Over 14 days: Sun up 96%, Earth in view 93%, both 93% of the time.
Survives the mission: the battery never drops below 140 Wh (lowest 586 Wh).
Longest darkness 12 h: that is the cold soak.
Battery used on this mission: 114 Wh of the 560 Wh it can use above its 140 Wh floor.
Battery model: power = panel power x visible Sun, whatever the Sun's direction (a sun-tracking array), so survival is an upper bound for fixed panels.
why: Darkest spell from 2028-09-14T20 UTC (12 h): terrain 11.1 km away blocks it (bearing 14 deg: skyline 1.67 deg, centre of the body at 1.48 deg).
Longest Earth blackout from 2028-09-14T10 UTC (23 h): it is below the Moon's own curvature (bearing 142 deg, horizon -1.33 deg).
